summary: We develop a transmon emitter/detector (TED) superconducting circuit combining a data transmon, a double transmon coupler (DTC), and a waveguide-coupled transmon to enable tunable single-photon emission and detection while preserving data-qubit coherence. In a meter-scale pitch-and-detect configuration, we demonstrate 60% detection of emitted Fock states with inferred 95% intrinsic detection efficiency, with both emission and detection protocols completing in ~2 µs each.
motivation: Scalable quantum networking requires compact, reconfigurable quantum communication interfaces that preserve quantum processor coherence while enabling entanglement distribution between heterogeneous nodes with frequency flexibility.
method: We exploit the recently developed DTC architecture to mediate parametric exchange interactions between a well-isolated data transmon and waveguide modes, using flux-driven modulation at the difference frequency $\omega_p = |\omega_w - \omega_d|$ to emit superposition states and detect incident Fock photons via a $|11\rangle \leftrightarrow |02\rangle$ transition. The sTED and mTED are connected via coaxial cable and circulator, with the composite system modeled using SLH formalism incorporating transmission loss $\eta$.
result: At optimal tuning, the mTED achieves 95% intrinsic detection fidelity with $T_1 = 81(35)$ µs for $Q_d$ and $\gamma_m = 11.2(1) \times 10^6 \text{ s}^{-1}$ for $Q_w$, detecting 60% of incident photons end-to-end (35% loss attributed to 1 m coaxial cable and circulator); the $Q_w$ transition frequency is tunable over ~300 MHz via static flux bias with $g_p = 0.584(6)\gamma_m$ for emission and $g_p = 0.259(3)\gamma_m$ for detection.
